We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 6 reactions using templates in order: ['20810','2895','1914397','1914398','1914399','74054'].

We have applied first four templates, got products (precursors). Need to continue with template 1914399 then 74054 to reach final target. The route must be a JSON tree starting from target molecule (the given SMILES). Each reaction node with template_id and children being precursor molecules (type mol). For each step we need to include the precursors from apply_template results.

We have results:

Step1 (template 20810) applied to target gives precursors: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F') Wait the result tuple: first is product? Actually apply_template returns list of tuples of precursor SMILES? The result shows a tuple of two strings: first is something, second is O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F. So the retrosynthetic step splits target into two fragments: a sulfonyl chloride aromatic? The target had O=S(N...)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O. So the template likely replaces sulfonyl chloride with sulfonamide. So precursors are the amine fragment and sulfonyl chloride fragment.

Thus step1: target -> reaction 20810 -> children: mol1 = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" and mol2 = "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F". Good.

Step2 (template 2895) applied to mol1 gives precursor: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1',) only one precursor? It returns a tuple with one string. So reaction 2895 transforms the amine fragment, maybe nitration. So step2: mol1 -> reaction 2895 -> child mol = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". (Only one precursor, meaning other reagents maybe implicit.)

Step3 (template 1914397) applied to that gives precursors: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1', 'O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2'). So split into two fragments: a protected amine (tert-butyl carbamate?) and a brominated aromatic fused ring.

Step4 (template 1914398) applied to the aromatic fragment gives precursors: ('BrBr', 'O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2'). So splits into BrBr (bromine molecule?) and a core aromatic fused ring with nitro.

Now need template 1914399 applied to something. Likely to the core fragment "O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". Let's apply.
